headline: Dave Portnoy and Barstool Sports Removed from Fox Sports’ ‘Big Noon Kickoff’ College Football Show

sources.excerpt: Dave Portnoy and Barstool Sports’ partnership with Fox Sports is coming with a shakeup. Barstool will no longer appear on the network’s “Big Noon Kickoff” ahead of college football games on Saturday, with Portnoy confirming a report by The Athletic. Portnoy, along with other Barstool personalities, has been a part of Fox Sports’ college football coverage for just over a year. According to The Athletic, the primary factors of the decision came down to challenges stemming from trying to tie together the more traditional programming from Fox with Barstool’s edgy persona, given the network’s partnership with the Big Ten. Portnoy, an alum and booster for Michigan, has faced flak over being at Ohio State home games. Reports last season even indicated that Portnoy was banned from entering Ohio Stadium, though the university officially denied that he was. In a post on X Friday evening, Portnoy was more direct, calling out Ohio State head coach Ryan Day in an expletive-laden message. “Ohio State and Ryan Day bitched and moaned to the Big 10 and threatened Fox till they had no choice,” Portnoy wrote. “Juice wasn’t worth the squeeze and frankly I don’t blame them. Huge dollars at stake and you have Cryin Ryan throwing temper tantrums and making threats every few days on something I said. I always knew Ryan Day was soft but holy s–t even I didn’t realize he was this soft. The Barstool College Football will continue on. Maybe we’ll even see you in Columbus where contrary to popular belief most fans love the rivalry and aren’t p—–s like Cryin Ryan.”

Dave Portnoy and Barstool Sports will no longer appear on Fox Sports’ “Big Noon Kickoff,” sources briefed on the decision told The Athletic. Reached by phone Friday night, Portnoy, a Michigan alum and booster, claimed Ohio State and coach Ryan Day were behind the decision after they repeatedly complained to Fox Sports’ top executives about his presence. Portnoy said he and Fox Sports maintain an excellent relationship, but the Buckeyes were unrelenting. According to Portnoy, Ohio State informed Fox Sports that if he was part of the program last week in Columbus, it would offer no access to Fox Sports personnel. “Ohio State has relentlessly complained to Fox,” Portnoy said. When reached for comment, Ohio State officials referred all inquiries to Fox Sports, which also declined comment. The school has previously disputed reports that it interfered with Portnoy’s presence on Fox’s shows. Portnoy and fellow top Barstool personalities, like Dan “Big Cat” Katz, have been a part of Fox’s college football program for a little more than a year. Fox Sports executives had envisioned them representing the voice of the fans. The sources briefed on the matter, speaking on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, said there wasn’t one specific reason for the decision’s abrupt timing. But the constant challenge of trying to unite Fox Sports’ more traditional show with Barstool’s persona proved unsustainable. Portnoy has faced disputes over his presence at Ohio State home games, with reports last year stating he was banned from entering the stadium. Ohio State athletic director Ross Bjork refuted those reports multiple times. Portnoy’s schtick is to rile up opponents, which often includes taunts. With Fox Sports’ partnership with the Big Ten, his presence ended up not being worth the hassle. “The juice wasn’t worth the squeeze,” Portnoy said. “Fox Sports CEO Eric Shanks and I have a good relationship.” The decision does not affect “Wake-Up Barstool,” the Barstool Sports show that airs on FS1 every weekday. The two sides could also try to create other programs. The Barstool addition was seen as a direct response to Pat McAfee joining ESPN’s “College GameDay.” McAfee, who started his post-NFL career at Barstool, has developed into the center of ESPN’s pregame show with his personality. McAfee, though, was not banned from entering stadiums. The incongruence between what Fox Sports usually does and Barstool’s style just proved too much to manage, and beginning Saturday in Minnesota, Fox Sports will only feature its main desk of Urban Meyer, Matt Leinart, Brady Quinn, Mark Ingram II and host Rob Stone.

Fox's experiment of adding Dave Portnoy and Barstool Sports to the "Big Noon Kickoff" college football pregame show appears to be done. According to The Athletic's Andrew Marchand, Portnoy and Barstool Sports will no longer appear on Fox's Saturday college football pregame show. Portnoy and Barstool personalities, such as "Big Cat", have appeared on the pregame show since the start of last season, with Portnoy making most of the appearances alongside Urban Meyer, Matt Leinart, Brady Quinn, Mark Ingram, Chris Fallica and Rob Stone. Portnoy, a well-known Michigan alum and donor, went on X, formerly Twitter, on Friday night to "sum up" his side of the story, noting that he had not seen Marchand's article and did not receive a call for a quote. "Ohio State and Ryan Day (expletive) and moaned to the Big 10 and threatened Fox till they had no choice. Juice wasn't worth the squeeze, amd [sic] frankly I don't blame them. Huge dollars at stake and you have Cryin Ryan throwing temper tantrums amd [sic] making threats every few days on something I said. I always knew Ryan Day was soft, but holy (expletive) even I didn't realize he was this soft," Portnoy wrote. "The Barstool College Football will continue on. Maybe we’ll even see you in Columbus, where, contrary to popular belief, most fans love the rivalry and aren't (expletive) like Cryin Ryan." Marchand noted that sources briefed on the decision said there wasn’t one specific reason for Portnoy and Barstool Sports' removal heading into the network's Week 5 "other than the constant challenge of trying to unite Fox Sports’ more traditional show with Barstool's persona proved unsustainable." Fox announced in July 2025 that it had agreed to a partnership deal with Barstool Sports that brought Portnoy to the "Big Noon Kickoff" desk and created "Wake-Up Barstool," a Barstool daily sports talk show that airs on Fox Sports 1 from 8 to 10 a.m. ET. Marchand noted that "Wake-Up Barstool" is not expected to be impacted by the "Big Noon Kickoff" shakeup. "Big Noon Kickoff" is set to kick off at 10 a.m. ET on Saturday, Oct. 3 from the University of Minnesota ahead of the Golden Gophers' Big Ten home opener against Michigan.
